Resolves #21700

A multi-card selection now lands as one block in board order, starting at the drop slot, whichever of its cards the drag held. The drag stack's badge shows how many cards it carries. The held card still takes the slot and stays on top of the stack. The cards above it in board order go in front of it, and the rest follow it. `getBoardRecords` reads board order once for both the stack's other cards and the commit. It replaces the column loop in `getSelectedDragRecords`, so `SortZone.mjs` ends one line shorter.

Evidence: L3 (Playwright unit + e2e, headless Chromium) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-4). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `SortZone.spec.mjs` "a multi-selection dragged by its middle card lands in board order, the block starting at the slot". It is red on dev (held card first) and green here. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `SortZone.spec.mjs` "multi-selection proxy vdom: the stack draws the lead and at most four clones, and its badge shows the total", for 2, 3, 5 and 7 cards. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the existing contiguous-drop arm is unchanged and green (one `moveCard` per record under `isNormalizing`, one `cardsMove`). |
| AC-4 | The rule is stated in the JSDoc of the class, `getDragProxyConfig`, `getBoardRecords` and `processDragEnd`. CI-covered: the board unit family and `test/playwright/e2e/board/`. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The badge's text color is now `var(--neo-board-background)`, not `#ffffff`. White on neo-dark's mint accent was hard to read, and the badge now appears on every multi-card drag. In all five themes the accent sits opposite the board background in lightness.

## Test Evidence

Locally, the board unit family passed 175/175 and `test/playwright/e2e/board/` passed 32/32. I also drove `board/basic`, dragging the third of five selected cards into Review. Here they landed as Design, Build, Review, Test, Refine; on dev they landed as Review, Design, Build, Test, Refine.

The same five-card drag on `examples/board/basic`, whole page at 1440 × 900. The selection is Backlog's first five cards, and the drag holds the third (Review the login form) over Review. The frames are linked from the evidence ref `grace/21700-review-frames` at `6afa8c2926`, which leaves this PR's head alone.

Frame critique: each whole page, frame by frame.
- dev shows the stack over Review's slot with no number. Backlog's four other selected cards stand ghosted, and nothing on the page says how many cards travel.
- head adds the "5" badge on the stack's corner in both themes: dark ink on mint in neo-dark, and light ink on teal in neo-light.
- The rest of the page is the same in both: the Backlog ghosts, Review's one-card slot, the In progress 6/5 WIP mark, and the table below.
- The clones stay translucent, so the board shows through under them. That translucency is the stack's design, which its author kept on #21631 (comment 7055222547).
